its stage-level closure is about 360 stages across about 54 roadmaps

judgements.reason: Every Hodge milestone is already a theorem in the baseline (isInternal_piece, Semisimple.complementedLattice, Mixed/Strictness, PeriodDomain.finsum_h_eq_finrank), so only companion API is left; Multiquadratic still owes the ambiguous class-number formula and the ordinary-class-group form of Gal(K_gen/K) = Cl(K)/Cl(K)^2, which are genuine unproved targets.

ConformalMapping has six of seven layers complete and only the global prescribed-polygon Schwarz-Christoffel statement open, with its integrand, boundary values and asymptotics already in SchwarzChristoffel/*; Multiquadratic has two layers still open, the ambiguous class-number formula and the ordinary genus-field isomorphism, the second stacked on the first.

RootSystems still owes two theorems, injectivity of weylCoxeterHom (the half of Tits' theorem Coxeter/Presentation.lean explicitly leaves open, and the roadmap's hardest) and Matsumoto's theorem in its lift form; ConformalMapping owes only the global Schwarz-Christoffel polygon theorem on top of complete L0-L5.

ProfiniteCohomology has four whole layers untouched and stacked - all-degree cohomology with its snake long exact sequence (L10), cohomological dimension (L11), the Alexander-Whitney graded cup product (L12) and the Evens norm (L13) - plus gaps in L0-L9; RootSystems needs only Tits injectivity and Matsumoto on top of a classification, chamber theory and root data that are already in the library.

AdelicAlgebraicGroups must first have a general theory of connected reductive groups over a field (the baseline has no IsReductive, Borel or relative root system, only GL_n), then local topologies and integral models, then its own six layers ending in Siegel-set reduction theory and Tamagawa measures; ProfiniteCohomology sits directly on Mathlib's continuousCohomology with ten of its fourteen layers already partly built.

LocallyAnalyticDistributions stacks one prerequisite roadmap (Iwasawa algebras and bounded p-adic measures, with Mathlib's Amice transform on Z_p already there) under five layers of p-adic functional analysis; AdelicAlgebraicGroups needs the entire reductive-group theory over a field and over local fields before AA.0 can even be stated, and then reduction theory, Weil's integration formula and strong approximation.

Both stack a mostly-absent substrate: LocallyAnalyticDistributions needs Iwasawa algebras, locally analytic Banach spaces, the unbounded Amice transform and affinoid character spaces (no Tate or affinoid algebra exists in the baseline); QuadraticFormInvariants needs the Witt ring, the Hasse invariant, the dyadic local classification, Br(K) = H^2 by crossed products and Stiefel-Whitney classes, and on top of that exactly the untouched Layers 9-13 of ProfiniteCohomology plus the local-fields and semisimple-algebra roadmaps, which is the longer stack.

QuadraticFormInvariants is field-theoretic and already has square classes, Witt decomposition, Cartan-Dieudonne and the quaternion Brauer classes in the library; AbelianSchemes must first build algebraic spaces, Hilbert/Picard representability and Artin criteria (there is no AlgebraicSpace or AlgebraicStack anywhere in the baseline) and p-divisible groups with Grothendieck-Messing, before its own dual-abelian-scheme and Serre-Tate layers.

Neron models consume AbelianSchemes A1-A3 wholesale and then add formal/adic geometry and p-adic Hodge comparison plus six layers of their own - the smoothening theorem, component groups, semistable reduction, Raynaud uniformisation and Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich; the stage closure is 135 stages against 56, with 92 stages needed by Neron models that abelian schemes do not need.

EllipticCurveModularity's dependency closure strictly contains the Neron-model closure (it needs Neron models through Faltings' isogeny theorem) and adds full Serre modularity, modularity lifting, Galois deformation rings, potential modularity and ModularCurvesPartII on top: 343 further stages with nothing on the Neron side that modularity does not also need.

EllipticCurveModularity's closure strictly contains ShimuraCompactifications' - every Shimura-data, PEL and toroidal stage is already inside it - and adds ClassicalSerreModularity, GL2ModularityLifting, the Galois deformation roadmaps, Faltings finiteness, Neron models and ModularCurvesPartII on top.

WeilConjectures must build etale cohomology from nothing (no etale site or l-adic sheaf exists in the baseline) with the six operations, Poincare duality, perverse sheaves and Deligne's weights, plus Lefschetz pencils and rigid cohomology; ShimuraCompactifications needs the adelic/reductive-group, Shimura-data and PEL stack, which is comparable but smaller - 86 stages unique to Weil against 59 unique to the compactifications.

IgusaVarieties needs the whole Weil-side apparatus (etale duality, weights) and on top of it perfectoid spaces, diamonds with their six operations, perfectoid Shimura varieties, PEL integral models and toroidal compactifications, then its own Igusa-tower, affineness and semiperversity layers: 279 stages it needs that WeilConjectures does not, against 35 the other way.

Hodge has no unproved milestone left - the internal direct sum, polarizable semisimplicity, Deligne strictness and the Hodge-number partition are all in TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge - while ConformalMapping still owes the global Schwarz-Christoffel theorem, its one open layer.

The two share the Shimura, perfectoid and etale machinery, but EllipticCurveModularity adds 22 further roadmaps on top - Serre modularity, modularity lifting, global and local deformation rings, potential modularity, Faltings and ModularCurvesPartII - against the five (perfectoid Shimura varieties, Hodge-Tate subgroups, completed cohomology) that are special to Igusa: 171 extra stages against 57.

IgusaVarieties requires ShimuraCompactifications C4 and C5 outright and then adds perfectoid spaces, diamonds and their six operations, perfectoid Shimura varieties, Hodge-Tate period maps, endoscopic transfer and its own eight layers: 275 stages it needs beyond the compactification roadmap, against 4 the other way.

Hodge's four milestones are all proved and only companion API (a bundled pure category, the abelian structure on the mixed category) is left; RootSystems still needs injectivity of weylCoxeterHom, which its own document calls the single hardest theorem in the roadmap, and Matsumoto's theorem.

ProfiniteCohomology has Layers 10-13 entirely unbuilt and stacked on one another - all-degree cohomology and its long exact sequence, cohomological dimension, the graded cup product, the Evens norm - plus unfinished business in Layers 0-9; Multiquadratic needs the ambiguous class-number formula and the ordinary form of the genus-field isomorphism on foundations that are already complete.

Neron models need abelian schemes, and under them algebraic spaces and Picard representability, plus formal geometry and p-adic Hodge theory, before any of their six layers: 135 stages across 25 roadmaps; AdelicAlgebraicGroups needs the reductive-group theory and then six layers of adelic analysis, 15 stage-level dependencies across 5 roadmaps.

WeilConjectures needs essentially everything abelian schemes need (Deligne's weight theory imports them) and then the whole etale-cohomological apparatus that the baseline lacks entirely - six operations, duality, perverse sheaves, Weil II purity, Lefschetz pencils and rigid cohomology - before rationality and RH can even be stated.

QuadraticFormInvariants consumes ProfiniteCohomology's Kummer theory, all-degree cohomology, graded cup product and Evens norm - precisely the layers ProfiniteCohomology has not begun - and then adds the Witt ring, the Hasse invariant, the dyadic local classification, Br(K) = H^2 by crossed products, Stiefel-Whitney classes and the Scharlau transfer, plus the local-fields and semisimple-algebra roadmaps.

Neron models sit on abelian schemes, algebraic spaces, formal geometry and p-adic Hodge theory - 135 stages across 25 roadmaps, none of that substrate present in the baseline; LocallyAnalyticDistributions stacks one prerequisite roadmap and five layers of p-adic functional analysis on top of Mathlib's Mahler basis and bounded Amice transform.

EllipticCurveModularity's closure strictly contains the abelian-scheme closure and adds roughly 420 further stages - Serre modularity, modularity lifting, deformation rings, Faltings, modular curves, Shimura varieties - whereas abelian schemes stop at algebraic spaces, p-divisible groups and their own seven layers.

Both are within a theorem or two of the library, but RootSystems owes two unproved milestones, injectivity of weylCoxeterHom (its own hardest theorem, with only surjectivity proved) and Matsumoto's theorem, while Multiquadratic's remaining work is the ambiguous class-number formula and the ordinary reading of a genus-field isomorphism whose narrow form is already proved.
